findings: Coarse oval dark scale centres made the skin look too rounded and repetitive.

changes: Use smaller, more varied angular scales with restrained centre darkening, re-view final body/head renders, and pass current source/GLB/browser gates.

visual_checks.anatomy: pass: deep angular body, separate raised trigger and posterior dorsal, no invented broad pelvic fins
visual_checks.surface: pass: varied angular olive scales with restrained dark centres and thirty small forward-curving peduncle thorns in five rows per flank
visual_checks.head: pass: pale bare muzzle, thick lips, dark cheek/eye area and shallow eye-to-snout relief
visual_checks.fins: pass: dark-edged broad rear dorsal/anal, rounded pectorals and caudal fork
visual_checks.surface_contact: pass: source and actual imported GLB retain five-phase fin-root contact
visual_checks.motion: pass: locally hinged median/pectoral strokes and body/tail cycle survive GLB import with matching endpoints
visual_checks.browser: pass: exact draft GLB swims, pauses and disposes at desktop/mobile widths

limitations: Original photo-informed Balistoides viridescens artwork, not a scanned specimen.
The trigger is posed raised; locking mechanics and fine teeth are simplified. Swimming is artist-tuned.
